=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:2555-2557 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The post-dispatch registration-list read treats rate-limit exit code 75 as a generic failure and continues polling without waiting for the rate limit to reset.
  WHY: A sustained rate limit on this endpoint can exhaust the 90-second registration window and fail the retry dispatch even when a review run has already been dispatched.
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:2592-2594 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The adopted-run status read treats rate-limit exit code 75 as a generic failure and continues polling without waiting for the rate limit to reset.
  WHY: A sustained rate limit on this endpoint can exhaust the retry deadline without observing the adopted review run's completion.
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:2281-2303 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The rate-limit wait helper silently uses the 60-second default when the `/rate_limit` request fails or its payload is malformed or stale.
  WHY: Operators cannot tell whether the wait came from GitHub's reported reset or the fallback, making it harder to diagnose deadline consumption and tune the gate.
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:gh_api_with_retry, lines ~2156-2184 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: When a rate-limit error occurs after earlier failed attempts, the success-path cleanup removes accumulated stderr and the dedicated warning reports only the current attempt's stderr.
  WHY: Operators investigating a later `pr_state_check_failed` may have less diagnostic context than the previous cumulative warning provided.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: Phase 4b should wait out rate limits for every read inside the poll loop; the stated non-goal exempts one-shot reads outside that loop.
  expected_change_site: .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml, Phase 4b registration-list and adopted-run status reads around lines 2555-2557 and 2592-2594
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: Both reads treat exit code 75 as a generic failure and continue without waiting; the registration-list read can exhaust the 90-second registration window, and the adopted-run status read can exhaust the retry deadline without observing completion.
- requirement: Behavioral tests should exercise rate-limit handling for the adopted-run status and registration-list endpoints.
  expected_change_site: tests/test_test_and_mark_stable_review_blocked_budget.py, `_STUB_GH` and its behavioral tests
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  EVIDENCE: `_STUB_GH` applies `limited` only to `/pulls/<number>`; `/actions/workflows/...` and `/actions/runs/<id>` never return rate-limit errors, so the tests do not exercise those poll-loop reads under rate-limit pressure.

=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:2555-2557 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The post-dispatch registration-list read treats rate-limit exit code 75 as a generic failure and continues polling without waiting for the rate limit to reset.
  WHY: A secondary rate limit during the 90-second registration window can exhaust the deadline and fail with `retry_dispatch_failed` while a review run has already been dispatched.
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:2592-2594 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The adopted-run status read treats rate-limit exit code 75 as a generic failure and continues polling without waiting for the rate limit to reset.
  WHY: A sustained rate limit on the run-status endpoint can consume the retry deadline and produce `retry_timeout` while the adopted review run is still `in_progress`.
- Requirement: The plan says "the poll loop can wait for the reset within its deadline rather than count the read as an unresolvable PR" and the `gh_api_with_retry` wrapper returns exit code 75 so the poll loop can distinguish rate limits from other failures. This mechanism applies to every `gh_api_with_retry` call inside the poll loop, not only the PR-state read. The plan's non-goal limits rate-limit-wait coverage to "one-shot reads outside the poll loop."
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml, in the poll loop: the registration-list read (lines 2555-2557) and the adopted-run status read (lines 2592-2594), and the test stub (tests/test_test_and_mark_stable_review_blocked_budget.py, `_STUB_GH`) to exercise rate-limit handling on those endpoints.
  Evidence of absence: Both branches use plain `if ! ... gh_api_with_retry ...` with no rate-limit branch. The test stub (lines 329-336) never checks `limited` for `/actions/workflows/` or `/actions/runs/<id>` endpoints; all behavioral tests rely on those endpoints never being rate-limited.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:phase4b_rate_limit_wait_seconds, lines 2281-2303 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When GET `/rate_limit` fails or returns malformed or stale data, the helper silently falls through to the 60-second default, without distinguishing that fallback from a wait derived from the rate-limit response.
  WHY: On a secondary rate limit, the helper can sleep for 60 seconds even when the limit resets sooner, consuming time within the deadline; operators cannot tell from the notice whether the wait used GitHub's reset or the fallback.
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:gh_api_with_retry, lines ~2156-2184 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: When an attempt fails for a non-rate-limit reason and a later attempt succeeds, accumulated stderr from earlier failures is removed; when a later attempt is rate-limited, accumulated stderr is removed and the dedicated warning contains only that attempt's stderr.
  WHY: An operator investigating a later `pr_state_check_failed` may not see the full attempt sequence that the previous cumulative warning would have captured.
- Requirement: "The stable release gate's Phase 4b now waits out GitHub rate limits instead of failing as if GitHub were down." (changelog headline, restating the PR goal) — applied to every `gh api` read inside the Phase 4b poll loop, not only the PR-state read.
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml, line 2592-2594 (the adopted-run status read `if ! RETRY_RUN_JSON=$(gh_api_with_retry "repos/${TEST_REPO}/actions/runs/${RETRY_RUN_ID}"); then ... continue`).
  Evidence of absence: `gh_api_with_retry` now returns rc=75 for a rate-limited attempt and the adopted-run read treats 75 like any other failure, continuing until the 25-minute deadline expires with `retry_timeout`.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- Requirement: "Behavioural tests ... cover the recovery, the deadline expiry, PR closure, and the unchanged breaker" and "Contract assertions: the rate-limit branch precedes the unknown branch, the breaker counter is untouched there, and the wait is capped by DEADLINE." (plan, Files & Modules > Tests)
  Expected change site: tests/test_test_and_mark_stable_review_blocked_budget.py, the `_STUB_GH` script and its test consumers.
  Evidence of absence: `_STUB_GH` rate-limits only the `/pulls/<PR_NUMBER>` branch. The adopted-run and post-dispatch registration-list endpoints are never rate-limited by the stub, and the contract test does not cover generic `if ! gh_api_with_retry ... then continue` patterns elsewhere in the loop.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- Requirement: Phase 4b should “wait out GitHub rate limits instead of treating them as an outage” while polling for the retry review run.
  Expected change site: `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml`, post-dispatch registration polling around lines 2555-2557 and adopted-run status polling around lines 2592-2594.
  Evidence of absence: `gh_api_with_retry` returns exit code 75 for rate-limited responses, but only `fetch_pr_state` maps that code to `rate_limited` and invokes the wait path. The post-dispatch run-list and run-status reads handle 75 as generic failures and continue without waiting. A sustained limit on the run-list read can expire the 90-second registration window; a sustained limit on the run-status read can expire the retry deadline without observing the run’s completion.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:lines 2555-2557 and 2592-2594 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The registration-list read (`gh_api_with_retry "${RETRY_RUNS_QUERY}"`) and adopted-run status read (`gh_api_with_retry "repos/${TEST_REPO}/actions/runs/${RETRY_RUN_ID}"`) treat rate-limit exit code 75 as generic failure and continue to the next 15-second iteration without calling `phase4b_rate_limit_wait_seconds`.
  WHY: If either Actions API endpoint is rate-limited while PR-state reads remain available, the loop can continue until `retry_timeout` without waiting for the limit to reset.
- Requirement: "Behavioural tests ... cover the recovery, the deadline expiry, PR closure, and the unchanged breaker" and the PR description claims that "the poll loop can wait for the reset within its deadline rather than count the read as an unresolvable PR."
  Expected change site: tests/test_test_and_mark_stable_review_blocked_budget.py, `_STUB_GH` stub and the behavioral tests.
  Evidence of absence: The stub's `rate_limit` endpoint and `limited` flag apply only to `/pulls/<number>`. The `/actions/workflows/...` and `/actions/runs/<id>` endpoints never return rate-limit errors, so no test exercises either poll-loop read under rate-limit pressure.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
